objects.description: SHA-1 message-digest context structure holding the running state (5-word hash state), total processed bit/byte count, and a 64-byte working buffer for block processing. Used with SHA1Init, SHA1Update, SHA1Pad, and SHA1Final to compute SHA-1 digests.

functions.name: SHA1Init
functions.description: Initializes a SHA1_CTX for a new SHA-1 hash computation by setting internal state and counters. Typical usage: call once before any SHA1Update calls and before finalization.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a SHA1_CTX.
Must be called before SHA1Update, SHA1Pad, or SHA1Final on the same context.
The context should not be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: SHA1Pad
functions.description: Applies the SHA-1 padding to the message in the provided context. Usually invoked internally by SHA1Final; exposed for low-level control when finalizing a digest in multiple steps.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to an initialized SHA1_CTX (initialized via SHA1Init).
Should be called only after all input data has been provided via SHA1Update and before producing the final digest.
Once padding is applied, do not call SHA1Update on the same context unless reinitialized.

functions.name: SHA1Transform
functions.description: Core SHA-1 compression function that processes exactly one 64-byte block to update the 5-word state. Intended for low-level/internal use; most callers should use SHA1Update/SHA1Final instead.
requirements: The first argument must point to an array of 5 uint32_t words representing the current SHA-1 state; it will be updated in place.
The second argument must point to exactly SHA1_BLOCK_LENGTH (64) bytes of input data.
Both pointers must be non-null and correctly aligned for their types.
Processes exactly one block; the caller must handle message padding and length encoding if using this directly.

functions.name: SHA1Update
functions.description: Feeds arbitrary-length data into an ongoing SHA-1 hash computation. Can be called multiple times to process streaming input.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a SHA1_CTX previously initialized with SHA1Init.
If len > 0, the data pointer must be non-null and reference at least len bytes readable memory.
May be called multiple times before finalization; do not call after SHA1Final or SHA1Pad unless the context is reinitialized.
Behavior is stable for len == 0 (a no-op).

functions.name: SHA1Final
functions.description: Finalizes the SHA-1 computation, writing the 20-byte message digest to the provided buffer and cleaning up the context state as needed. After this call, the context typically must be reinitialized to hash new data.
requirements: digest must point to a writable buffer of at least SHA1_DIGEST_LENGTH (20) bytes.
ctx must be a valid, writable pointer to a SHA1_CTX that has been initialized with SHA1Init.
Must be called after all data has been provided via SHA1Update; it will perform any required padding.
Do not call SHA1Update on the same context after SHA1Final unless reinitialized with SHA1Init.

endpoints.name: SHA1Init
SHA1Pad
SHA1Update
SHA1Final
SHA1Transform

data_types.description: A buffer of raw bytes with no required encoding or structure. May contain any 0x00–0xFF values, including embedded NULs. Length can be zero or any positive size; consumers treat it as opaque binary data.
